skill.name: stripe-integration
skill.description: Implement Stripe checkout, subscriptions, webhooks, refunds, and customer payment method flows with secure payment patterns and Stripe API examples.
skill.summary: Build Stripe checkout, subscription, webhook, refund, and customer billing flows.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, placeholder URLs, dummy Stripe test keys, and ordinary Stripe object fields. No evidence of prompt injection or malicious exfiltration was found, but the webhook guidance includes incomplete manual signature verification and inline secret placeholders.

remediation.issue: Manual webhook signature helper omits Stripe header parsing and timestamp tolerance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the custom helper or replace it with Stripe.Webhook.construct_event or the official Stripe signature validation algorithm.

remediation.issue: Examples show Stripe API keys and webhook secrets as inline string placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or a managed secret store in every secret-handling example.

remediation.issue: The skill references extra resources and assets that are not present in this package.
remediation.suggestion: Either add the referenced files or remove those references so users do not assume missing production-ready assets exist.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Webhook Signature Verification Example
semantic_findings.description: The manual webhook verifier compares a payload HMAC to a provided signature. It omits Stripe's timestamped signed payloads and replay-protection checks. Users copying this helper could implement weaker webhook authentication than the official SDK path shown earlier.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 277-285 show a custom verifier that omits Stripe's signed payload format and timestamp tolerance. The risk is in implementation guidance rather than executable code, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Inline Webhook Secret Placeholder
semantic_findings.description: The webhook example sets the endpoint secret directly as a string placeholder. This can encourage hardcoded secrets in payment code if copied without a secret manager or environment variable.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 215 directly assigns a Stripe webhook secret placeholder to a variable in a security-sensitive example. It is documentation, not executable code, so risk depends on whether users copy it unchanged.

content.value_statement: Payment integrations require secure checkout, subscriptions, and webhook handling. This skill guides Stripe implementation patterns for billing flows, refunds, customer portals, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains hosted Checkout, Payment Intents, Setup Intents, subscriptions, and customer management.
Provides Python examples for checkout sessions, payment intents, subscriptions, portals, refunds, and disputes.
Shows webhook event handling with Stripe signature verification using the Stripe SDK.
Lists Stripe test cards and test-mode payment flow checks.
Covers idempotency, error handling, metadata, monitoring, PCI scope, and SCA practices.
limitations: It provides examples only and does not include runnable package files in this skill directory.
It focuses on Python and Flask patterns, not every Stripe SDK or frontend framework.
It uses placeholder URLs and keys that must be replaced before any deployment.
It does not design database schemas, access control, tax handling, or accounting workflows.

use_cases.title: Launch SaaS Subscriptions
use_cases.description: Add checkout, recurring billing, customer portal access, and cancellation handling for a SaaS product.

use_cases.title: Add One-Time Checkout
use_cases.description: Implement hosted Checkout or Payment Intent flows for product purchases with webhooks and confirmation handling.

use_cases.title: Review Payment Operations
use_cases.description: Plan refund, dispute, webhook retry, and idempotency practices before moving a Stripe integration to production.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads and payment operations teams

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Checkout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the stripe-integration skill to design a hosted Stripe Checkout flow for a one-time product purchase. Include backend steps, redirect URLs, webhook events, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Add Subscription Billing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the stripe-integration skill to plan monthly subscription billing for my application. Cover products, prices, customer creation, payment confirmation, portal access, and cancellation webhooks.

prompt_templates.title: Secure Webhook Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the stripe-integration skill to review my Stripe webhook design. Check signature verification, idempotency, event routing, retry behavior, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Marketplace Payouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the stripe-integration skill to outline a Stripe Connect marketplace payment flow. Include account onboarding, payment collection, transfers, refunds, disputes, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need Stripe Checkout for a digital course.
output: A hosted Checkout flow with one-time payment mode and product price setup.
Server-side session creation and success and cancel redirect planning.
Webhook confirmation for completed payments before course access is granted.
Test cases for successful, declined, and 3D Secure card flows.

output_examples.input: My SaaS needs subscriptions and a customer portal.
output: A subscription flow using products, recurring prices, customer records, and saved payment methods.
Customer portal guidance for plan changes, billing details, and cancellation handling.
Webhook events to update access after subscription changes and failed payments.

output_examples.input: I want to harden webhook handling before launch.
output: A review of signature verification, idempotency, retry behavior, and event routing.
Recommendations for logging payment failures, refunds, and disputes.
A launch checklist covering test mode, metadata, monitoring, and production secrets.

best_practices: Store Stripe API keys and webhook secrets in managed environment secrets, not source files.
Use Stripe SDK webhook verification and process events idempotently.
Test successful, declined, 3D Secure, refund, and subscription cancellation flows before production.
anti_patterns: Relying only on client-side payment success without server-side webhook confirmation.
Copying placeholder keys, URLs, or test data into production configuration.
Creating payment flows without retry, logging, metadata, or dispute handling plans.

faq.question: Does this skill handle raw card data?
faq.answer: No. It recommends Stripe-hosted Checkout or Stripe.js patterns that keep raw card data out of your server.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: Examples focus on Python and Flask, but the flow guidance maps to other Stripe SDKs.

faq.question: Can it help build subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers products, prices, subscription creation, saved payment methods, and customer portal sessions.

faq.question: Does it cover Stripe webhooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists important events and shows signature verification, idempotent processing, and retry-aware handlers.

faq.question: Is this a production-ready payment module?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance, not a drop-in audited module. You must adapt secrets, URLs, error handling, and compliance reviews.

faq.question: Does it support Stripe Connect?
faq.answer: It identifies marketplace flows as a use case, but the included examples focus on core payments and billing.
